A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEPTHOR work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. Corresponding material can be matched reliably, including the imaging explanation moved into v2's supplementary sections. The supplied v1 has no appended supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original DEPTHOR evaluations, retrained-model comparisons and ablations on Hypersim, ZJU-L5 and collected phone samples, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a PENet control result, supplementary qualitative ablations and failure cases.

M1.justification: The fusion/refinement architecture and loss remain unchanged. However, v2's shortened depth-encoder description omits v1's explicit max-pooling operation. The PDFs do not establish whether pooling was actually removed or merely left undocumented.

E1.justification: The principal datasets remain Hypersim, ZJU-L5, NYUv2 and collected Honor-phone samples. v2 adds limited illustrative coverage through an ARKitScenes ground-truth example in Figure 4 and an explicitly rotated-input failure case in Figure 12a.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Deltar simulation to the lightweight PENet* comparison; v1 reported Deltar simulation for full PENet and DEPTHOR, but only MIPI and the proposed simulation for PENet*. Main benchmark comparator membership is otherwise unchanged; the DAv2 labels rename existing comparators.

E3.justification: The reported random-anomaly settings change from approximately 1% noise points and 1% blank points to 5% each. Table 1 also adds a matched lightweight-PENet control under Deltar simulation. These are reported setting/design changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 11 adds real-sample PENet ablations isolating calibration shifts and non-Lambertian simulation effects (Figures 10–11), extending beyond v1's displayed quantitative simulation ablations. Section 12 adds dedicated failure analysis for excessive sensor anomalies and rotated-image semantic errors, substantially expanding robustness and failure evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing. The supplement adds training iterations, which do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–7 are retained. v2 adds PENet* with Deltar simulation: delta1 0.815, Rel 0.152 and RMSE 0.510, plus PENet computation figures and supplementary qualitative outcomes. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 9 adds explicit mathematical definitions and derivation of the dToF-to-RGB coordinate transformation and projection (Equations 5–10), previously described verbally. Existing method equations and the relocated imaging relation are unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same simulation strategy, MDE-integrating completion model and performance claims, including the 27%/18% and 23%/22% improvements. Local wording changes do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains stereo-ground-truth shifts through lens distortion and baseline mismatch, and argues for stereo supervision in challenging regions. The supplement newly discusses missing inputs mistaken for distant surfaces, excessive sensor anomalies and rotation-sensitive MDE errors, extending v1's ground-truth and runtime limitations.

D1.justification: Sections 7–10 supply substantial previously unavailable detail: four RTX 3090 GPUs, AdamW/OneCycle settings, approximately 230K iterations, batch size 12, projection formulas and sensor-specific simulation parameters. Stereo filtering and masking are also disclosed. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explanation of the first seven Table 2 rows' provenance and the small model's half-resolution MDE processing.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting optimization, software, simulation, stereo matching and odometry, including AdamW, PyTorch, TartanAir, FoundationStereo and IGEV++. The central positioning relative to depth completion, super-resolution and monocular estimation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact. v2 moves the imaging preliminary into the supplement, renumbers method subsections, edits several paragraphs, clarifies DAv2 terminology and adds acknowledgements and organized supplementary sections.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the model overview, individually labels the anomaly examples, relocates the imaging diagram and adds a ground-truth comparison plus six supplementary figures covering ablations, failures and additional predictions. Table headers and placement also change, with Table 1 gaining a control row.

improvement.justification: The added training details, matched PENet control, real-sample ablations and explicit failure cases improve reproducibility and assessment of the retained claims. Benefits are tempered by lost baseline provenance and inconsistencies in new documentation: the EWMAE directional average repeats east instead of including west, and the stated 928×714 padding conflicts with 1/32 downsampling. The net improvement is useful but limited.
